title: VeriRole: Verifiable Role-Awareness through Hint-Guided Reinforcement Learning
claim: Good responses must satisfy factual constraints while staying creative; naive outputs either accept false premises or become dull.
layout: Query on top, three response bubbles left, overlapping space diagram right
description: A pink query bubble at the top, with a user icon, says the user remembers the character mastering the Patronus Charm at 11. Below it are three stacked response bubbles. The blue one accepts the false premise in a playful voice and is marked with a red X. The green one corrects the age to 13 and adds vivid story detail, marked with a green check. The yellow one bluntly says 'No, I learned it when I was 13' and has a red X. A character avatar sits to the left. On the right, a dashed region labeled 'Possible Response Space' contains two overlapping zones. The blue Creative Space covers tone, diversity and emotion. The yellow Factual Space covers context, role requirement and profile. Their green overlap is the Ideal Response Space. Lines with dots link each bubble to its zone. The eye goes first to the colored bubbles and their check and X marks.
caption: An ideal response balances creative freedom with factual invariants. For the same query (e.g., a user incorrectly states Harry Potter learned the Patronus Charm at 11), a model might: (a) accept the false premise for narrative fluency; (b) produce a Dull but factually correct response; or (c) generate a response which is both factually accurate and creative.
abstract: Maintaining role-awareness in Role-Playing Conversational Agents (RPCAs) is a significant challenging, largely because the creative nature of role-playing makes it difficult to design verifiable reward signals for reinforcement learning (RL). To address this, we propose VeriRole, a new framework designed to enhance the role-awareness of agents through a structured, verifiable reasoning process. The core of our framework is a 'hint' mechanism, designed to first extract deterministic cues from the context, before the main response generation.Building on these hints, we introduce a Verifiable Role-Awareness Reward (VRAR) to provide a verifiable signal for role-awareness. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach. Our Qwen2.5-32B model, optimized with VeriRole, achieves an 18.9% and 4.55% increase in average scores on the RAIDEN and CharacterEval benchmarks, respectively. These results confirm that VeriRole can effectively quantify and improve role-awareness, leading to superior persona consistency and robustness. To ensure reproducibility, all prompts are detailed in the Appendix, and the associated training data has been made publicly available.
